chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Khayrān al-Khādim, who said:

I wrote to the man, asking him about a garment that wine and pork meat had come into contact with: may one perform salat (prayer) in it or not? For indeed our companions had differed concerning it. So he wrote: one must not perform salat (prayer) in it, for it is impure.

key_terms.أَصْحَابَنَا: our companions; the Shia community or scholars who differed on the issue
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْخَمْرُ: wine; an intoxicating substance mentioned as contaminating the garment
key_terms.رِجْسٌ: impure or filthy, indicating ritual impurity in this context
key_terms.لَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pork meat, cited here as a source of impurity

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a garment touched by wine or pork?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal question regarding a garment contaminated by wine and pork meat and whether salat (prayer) may be performed in it. The reply gives a clear ruling that salat (prayer) is not to be performed in such a garment because it is considered impure.
